column1: # Wormhole statics: which wormhole types a system of each class may hold.
# Read by the server (`wormhole::TABLE`, CP54a); header frozen in
# docs/content/schema.md §4. Edit and restart; no re-extract needed.
# Spec: docs/content/R-WH.md §6 (the rule G-WH) and §6.3 (these rows).
# The client ships NO statics (R-WH §6.1 [V]): nothing maps a system to its
# static. These rows are our rule, one per (source class, wormhole type):
# - class: the home system's effective wormhole class (1-6 J-space, 7 high,
#   8 low, 9 null [V constants]; a k-space system without a class takes its
#   band's, `wormhole::effective_class` [A]).
# - static_type_id: the wormhole type the slot may draw. Its lifetime and
#   masses are the type's own dogma attributes, read at runtime; none is
#   written here.
# - dest_class: the class the far end is drawn from. It must equal the
#   type's wormholeTargetSystemClass (1381); the loader drops a row whose
#   type contradicts it, or is not a wormhole (group 988), once typedata
#   carries the type.
# Membership is [I]: the client's two-object archetype-38 dungeons come in
# blocks of nine, one block per source class, each reaching classes 1-9 once
# (R-WH §6.1). Drawing uniformly among a class's rows is [A]. How many
# statics a class holds is a Rust const (`wormhole::statics_per_system`).
# Thera, frigate, Drifter and Pochven holes are left out of v1 (R-WH §1.3);
# adding one is a row here.
class
